system.name: RIBOSOME
system.one_liner: a system that offloads stateful per-packet processing from Tbps programmable switches to server memory over RDMA

components.name: programmable switch
components.role: the RIBOSOME switch that splits, stores, and later rebuilds packets around external compute/memory

components.name: splitter
components.role: separates each incoming packet's header from its payload

components.name: header storage
components.role: buffers headers so the switch can later reassemble packets in the intended order

components.name: rebuilder
components.role: reconstructs outgoing packets from stored headers and the data returned by external systems

components.name: multi-core NF server
components.role: runs the network function (here, a per-flow packet scheduler) on extracted headers across multiple cores

components.name: core 1
components.role: NF core processing flows A and B, forwarded on port 1

components.name: core 2
components.role: NF core processing flows C and D, forwarded on port 2

components.name: RDMA server
components.role: buffers payload data reachable via RDMA while headers are processed elsewhere

components.name: QP1
components.role: RDMA queue pair used for payload belonging to flows on this connection

components.name: QP2
components.role: a second active RDMA queue pair on the same RDMA server

content.key_idea: RIBOSOME implements per-flow packet schedulers by splitting headers to a multi-core NF server and payloads to RDMA-addressable server memory, then rebuilding ordered packets in the switch from both.
content.reading_order: Left to right along the switch's splitter-storage-rebuilder pipeline, with dashed arrows dropping down to the NF and RDMA servers and solid arrows returning back up.

summary: Figure 4 illustrates how RIBOSOME supports per-flow packet schedulers such as Reframer using a concrete example. The programmable switch's splitter separates each incoming packet's header from its payload; headers are sent to a multi-core NF server (dashed orange arrows) while header storage retains ordering information and issues RDMA reads to an RDMA server holding the payloads. In the example, four flows A, B, C, and D arrive on four ports; A and B are mapped to core 1 of the NF server and leave on port 1, while C and D are mapped to core 2 and leave on port 2. Both servers return their results to the switch's rebuilder over solid green arrows, which reconstructs and reorders the packets (AABB, CCDD) before they exit. The figure uses color-coded packet squares and dashed-versus-solid arrows to distinguish outbound from inbound traffic.
summary_zh: 图4展示RIBOSOME如何支持逐流调度：交换机将包头与载荷分离，包头送至多核NF服务器处理，载荷经RDMA读写存于RDMA服务器；两者结果回传后由rebuilder按流（A、B到端口1，C、D到端口2）重组转发。
notes: layout-proposal: switch-pipeline-with-two-offload-peers — a three-stage in-switch pipeline (splitter, header storage, rebuilder) hands off to two side-by-side external systems (multi-core NF server, RDMA server) via paired outbound/inbound arrows, rather than a radial hub-spoke.
